classification.difficultyReason: Part a requires reading the diagram to identify the 4.5 cm side as adjacent to θ and the 9 cm side as the hypotenuse, then forming and simplifying 4.5/9 to 1/2. Part b is scaffolded by the given cos 60° = 1/2 and needs a short inference that equal cosine ratios mean equal acute angles, so the angle is 60°. This is one routine linked procedure plus a light interpretive step. It is slightly above p12-q4, which only rearranges a cosine equation with the value supplied. It is below p14-q10, which chains Pythagoras with several exact-ratio evaluations across both acute angles.
